#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Chapter
 on Adam

**
¶2.
** Three great end
owments,
 each
 distinct from
 the others, were made
 manifest
 in the
 Most
 Ancient spiritual
 consciousness —
 the first truly
 human
 mind
. By
 virtue
 of these
,
 that
 consciousness was
 found to be no
bler and more excellent than any composite faculty
 dwelling
 in the internal mind
 or the external mind.

**
¶3.** The first
: The very
 lik
eness of the Divine
 Itself
 was implanted in the inmost of
 this consciousness. The hered
itary natural faculties that formed and
 fash
ioned the external mind shaped
 it according
 to the rad
iant
 pattern of divine order that had been displayed
 to
 them from the interior. By
 virtue of this, the form
 of that
 first
 spiritual
 consciousness was found to be surpass
ingly beautiful beyond any composite faculty
,
 whether
 of
 the
 internal mind
 or the external.


**¶4.** The
 second: That
 consciousness was organized in
 its interior
 structure
 through the primary
 wisdom proceeding from the celest
ial and
 natural
 degrees
 —
 the five fundamental capac
ities of spiritual perception. By virtue of
 this, its constitution
 was found to differ from the constitution
 of all
 other living
 forms
,
 since the form of every
 lesser
 perception
 differs
 one
 from another
. But
 in
 this
 first
 human
 consciousness
, the interior
 life
 was fitted
 perfectly
 over
 the true
 distribution of goods
 and truths in
 their
 proper order. Therefore it
 possessed
 understanding
 surpassing that
 of all other per
ceptions and natural
 aff
ections.

**¶5.
** The third: All
 divine teachings
 and
 interior
 counsel
s and the fixed im
press
 of every
 faculty
,
 both
 of
 the internal mind
 and the external,
 were gathered
 by
 the form
ative
 powers
 and sealed within
 it
. That
 first
 consciousness and
 its v
olitional counter
part became a dwelling and a
 hab
itation for all
 kn
owledges of good
 and truth in their ordered
 arrangement —
 for
 all successive
 states of spiritual
 life,
 all
 changes
 of condition
, and
 all completed
 cycles
.
 For
 the total
 pattern
 of the Grand
 Human is insc
ribed upon
 that
 consciousness
. By virtue of this, the
 whole
 internal
 mind
 and the whole external mind were moved on
 its
 account;
 cont
ention and disorder
 arose because
 of it
 between the goods flowing
 in
 from
 the Divine and the evils rising
 from the proprium. The
 goods
 drew
 it toward
 spiritual
 life,
 because
 of the Divine
 lik
eness and order
 placed within
 it; while the evils drew it
 toward
 spiritual death, so
 that the
 loves
 of self might
 exercise
 dominion through it and se
ize the ruling
 power
,
 and through
 it bring
 all
 things of
 heaven
 and earth into
 subjection.

**¶6
.** Furthermore, understand that the loves
 of self and the world —
 the ruling
 prop
rial powers — fash
ioned and
 determined
 this
 consciousness so that they might
 be masters through it and seize domin
ion,
 and
 they
 did
 so by
 means
 of seven complete
 designs
.

**¶7.**
 The first: It
 became the vessel
 of illumin
ation within
 their domain —
 a
 substitute
 for the wisdom
 of the Divine
 Truth
 that had manif
ested
 Itself to them from
 the interior. For all
 the
 prop
rial powers desired the likeness of that
 Divine Truth. Their aff
ections were drawn ir
resistibly toward it
.

**¶8.**
 The second: So that through
 this
 consciousness they might
 capture
 and contain wisdom
, and restrain and obstruct it
 from ascending
 and
 returning to its Divine
 source.

**¶9.
** The third: So that,
 on
 account of the Divine likeness placed
 within it, everything
 of the Divine dwelling
 above
 and below might
 be brought
 into hum
iliation — by
 explo
iting the correspondence
 of
 that
 spl
endor, that
 beauty,
 that apparent
 superi
ority. For in
 out
ward appearance it
 sur
passed all other
 aff
ections and perceptions.

**
¶10.** The fourth: It
 serves
 as a fixed
 sig
net and a
 new im
press
, so that all derivative
 states
 of life —
 every
 subsequent
 aff
ection and thought that
 would
 be generated
 — might be brought forth according
 to the
 same
 pattern.

**¶11.
** The fifth: That through
 it
 all
 the hidden
 and manifest capac
ities of
 every
 faculty
,
 internal
 and external, might be exercised and
 displayed;
 and that through
 it the prop
rial powers might order
 the whole of
 existence
, and everything be
 made
 subject
 within
 it.

**¶12.
** The sixth: That a
 great protection might come
 to them through the Divine lik
eness placed within it — for
 so
 long
 as the Divine
 image
 remained
,
 even
 the ruling
 prop
rial powers could
 not be
 destroyed,
 and
 no spiritual
 judgment
 could be executed
 against them on
 account of that
 consciousness
.

**¶13.**
 The seventh: That it might become the
 chief and sovereign
 and ruling
 love
 over all aff
ections and perceptions, and through
 it the prop
rial powers might possess
 the kingdom
 entire
.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Three great things that are distinct were revealed in Adam the first human. Indeed, due to this, he was found to be better and more outstanding than the conjoined powers that are in heaven and on earth.

The first: The image of the exalted one was placed upon him. The creators and moulders of his body sealed him after the shining form of the image that had been displayed to them above. Indeed, due to this, the image of Adam was found to be surpassingly beautiful beyond any conjoined power above and below.

The second thing: Adam was shaped in his structure through the light of the first-born of heaven and [earth, and through the light of] the five sons. Indeed, due to this, his structure was found to differ from the structure of even the other creations; [sin]ce the form of all creations is different. As for Adam, the formation of his soul fits over the correct distribution of the elements. Therefore, he has intelligence surpassing that of the other creations and beasts.

The third are the teachings and counsels and the seal of all the powers above and below. The creators, who set him in order, gathered them and sealed them in him. Adam and his consort Eve became a dwelling and home for the signs of the zodiac and the stars; and the months, the days and the years. For the seal of the entire universe is stamped upon Adam. Indeed, due to this, heaven and earth moved because of him; trouble and disorder arose on his account between they that are good and they that are evil. So, the good induce him to life because of their image and shape placed upon him; while the [wi]cked were drawing him to death, so that they would have power through him and they would conceive the kingdom, and through him humiliate the entire universe.
Furthermore, understand that the rulers determined and formed Adam so that they would be masters through him and conceive the kingdom because of seven things.

The first: He became the enlightener in their creation; instead of the light of the image of the Ambassador who had displayed himself to them above. For they all desired the likeness of the image of the Ambassador. Their heart was drawn after it.
The second: So that they would scoop up the light through him and restrain and obstruct it from its ascent to the heights.

The third: So that because of the image of the Ambassador that is placed upon him the entirety of the divine that is above and below would be humiliated; on account of the likeness of the splendour, of the beauty of his superiority. For he is superior in his appearance to all creatures.
The fourth: He is a seal-ring and a new impression, so that all births who will be begotten might be brought forth after his seal.

The fifth: That might be displayed through him all the skil[ls] of the powers, they above and below, secret and manifest; and that they might determine through him the totality, and every thing be revealed in him.

The sixth: That there would come to be a great protection for them through the image of the exalted one that was placed upon him; for as the heavenly would [behold the image upon him, they would not destroy] even rulers; and no evil thing would be done to them on account of Adam.
The seventh: That he might become chief and king and master over all creatures; and they might conceive the kingdom through him.
